findings.title: TemplateApiExtractor silently drops the source context
findings.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/extract.rs:228-243 builds the TemplateApiExtractor request with model, template, scrubbed text, tool payload, and retry feedback, but no `context`, even though `ExtractRequest.context` is declared at crates/clio-write/src/extract.rs:42-45. The chat adapter does include the field at crates/clio-write/src/extract_chat.rs:126-134, so the omission is specific to the template path.
findings.recommendation: Add the bounded, scrubbed context field to the template request and add a transport assertion that every extractor implementation receives the caller's context.

resolution.how: Fixed in crates/clio-write/src/extract.rs: TemplateApiExtractor body now carries the caller's context as scrubbed untrusted data ("context": req.context.as_deref().map(scrub_inline_secrets)). Transport assertion tests added: template_egress_carries_scrubbed_caller_context (body rides scrubbed context, secret text absent) and template_egress_omits_absent_context. Evidence: cargo test -p clio-write -> 168 passed; 0 failed.

findings.title: Public extraction entry points can send unvalidated context to an extractor
findings.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/parallel.rs:102-118 exposes `extract_chunks_parallel` with an unchecked context argument, and crates/clio-write/src/pipeline.rs:196-207 copies that argument into `ExtractRequest` without calling `validate_context`. The hosted chat adapter then interpolates it at crates/clio-write/src/extract_chat.rs:126-134. Only the raw-ingest wrapper validates at crates/clio-write/src/raw_ingest.rs:139-141, so direct callers can send empty or oversized context to the extraction seam.
findings.requirement_ref: FR-34; NFR-9; phase Task 1 (validate before extraction)
findings.recommendation: Make validation an invariant of every public extraction entry point (or construct `ExtractRequest` through a validating constructor), and add tests for empty, oversized, and instruction-like values on the direct paths.

resolution.how: Round 2 fix at the adapter boundary. crates/clio-write/src/extract.rs:228-236 (TemplateApiExtractor::extract) and crates/clio-write/src/extract_chat.rs:290-298 (ChatExtractor::extract) now call clio_types::validate_context on req.context before building any request body, so a direct caller cannot egress an empty or oversized context even when it bypassed the orchestration path; crates/clio-write/src/parallel.rs:127-144 validates the context once up front and fails every chunk with zero extractor calls; crates/clio-write/src/pipeline.rs extract_and_verify keeps its own validation. The reviewer's reproduction (direct TemplateApiExtractor::extract with a 4097-byte context returning result_is_ok=true and transport_calls=1) now fails closed with OutOfRange and no transport call. Tests: extract_tests::template_adapter_rejects_invalid_context_before_transport (its transport panics if reached), extract_chat_tests::chat_adapter_rejects_invalid_context_before_transport, parallel_tests::invalid_context_rejects_every_chunk_without_extractor_calls. Evidence: cargo test -p clio-write --lib -> all green; workspace make check green.

findings.title: belief_observe append replaces a differing context instead of rejecting it
findings.evidence: The belief contract requires an append to omit context or use the byte-identical stored value, but crates/clio-belief/src/observe.rs:234-235 routes an existing identity to `append_to_existing` and :305-311 forwards any supplied context to `append_confidence_with_context`. That API explicitly replaces the sealed context at crates/clio-store/src/belief_store.rs:56-72 and crates/clio-store/src/belief_tx.rs:149-155. A real MCP probe returned `outcome=appended` for a different context, and `belief_history` exposed only the replacement. The documented correction escape is also unavailable: crates/clio-compliance/src/correct.rs:181-186 rejects belief targets.
findings.requirement_ref: FR-34; §4.10 belief append rule; phase Task 1/AC-100606-09
findings.recommendation: Reject a differing context during belief append, preserve the old value for audit reconstruction, and provide an authorized belief-context correction operation before allowing replacement.

resolution.how: Round 3 fix of the four residual defects. (1) The correction audit no longer retains the sealed prior envelope: belief_context_correction_detail lost its cipher parameter and the prior_context_cipher field (crates/clio-store/src/belief_store.rs), both backends' correct_belief_context stop passing it, and the compliance test now asserts the field is ABSENT while the prior_/new presence/length/hash stats remain (correct_context_tests::belief_context_correction_changes_only_context_and_records_no_prior_cipher). (2) The MCP correct schema no longer contradicts the runtime: required = ["item_id","reason"], and new_value's description states it is required for item/attribute corrections and MUST be omitted for belief context-only corrections (a non-empty new_value with a belief correction is rejected) - pinned by context_read_schema_tests::correct_schema_requires_reason_but_not_new_value. (3) A context-only correction is now journaled and relayable: every domain-record equal-state apply branch returns Applied instead of Duplicate, so apply.rs journals the mutation and the pull path (which serves from the durable journal, server.rs handle_pull -> journal_list_since) can relay it to a third node; proven by apply_records_selfheal_tests::belief_context_only_correction_applies_and_journals (Applied + journal_get is Some + no conflict). (4) The belief change stamp is monotonic: the append UPDATEs in belief_tx.rs (SQLite MAX / Postgres GREATEST) and both correction UPDATEs never move updated_at backwards (MAX/GREATEST(COALESCE(updated_at, created_at), candidate)); sqlite/pg_belief_change_stamp_never_regresses_past_older_appends prove an append with an as_of older than the correction stamp cannot regress the stamp and the real feed_beliefs still selects the row. Evidence: cargo test -p clio-store --lib belief 35 passed; cargo test -p clio-sync 110 passed; cargo test -p clio-compliance 135 passed. Round 4 correction: three belief-path doc sites and the migration guide still claimed the prior sealed context was reconstructable through audit_trail, contradicting the hash-only rule this resolution describes. The code was already correct, so the prose was corrected, not the behavior: correct.rs, correct_context_tests.rs and context_correct_tests.rs (clio-mcp) now state that the audit keeps presence/length/hash only and the prior value is not retained, and docs/source-context-and-migration.md says the same.

findings.title: Persona updates can replace or clear context without an audited correction
findings.evidence: On a normal stable upsert without context, crates/clio-persona/src/stable.rs:163-176 creates a new version with `context: None`; crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_persona.rs:79-103 closes the old version and inserts the context-free new version, so `persona_get` loses the prior context. On a preference observation with a new context, crates/clio-persona/src/observe.rs:178-195 passes it through, and the SQLite upsert at crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_persona.rs:123-131 replaces the stored context. A real probe observed the replacement on a later preference observation, with no correction audit. This conflicts with the ordinary-update preservation rule and the requirement that replacement be explicit and audited.
findings.recommendation: Preserve context on ordinary stable/preference updates, and route any replacement through an explicit audited correction that retains the prior value. Add tests for omitted context, changed context, and the audit trail.

resolution.how: Round 3 fix of the three remaining comment sites the round-2 pass missed: crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_persona.rs and crates/clio-store/src/postgres_persona.rs no longer claim the prior sealed ciphertext is retained in the audit detail, and the clio-persona observe.rs module header states the hash-only rule. All three now match the code (persona_audit_detail keeps presence/length/hash only, sqlite_persona/tx_write.rs:256-259). No behavior change; cargo test -p clio-persona 22 passed, clio-store --lib persona 28 passed.

findings.title: Subject erasure does not purge or make persona context unreadable
findings.evidence: Persona context is sealed under the bank key at crates/clio-store/src/persona_store.rs:126-147 and crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_persona.rs:156-162. Erasure selection only scans `items` at crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_erase_purge.rs:30-50 (and the PostgreSQL equivalent at crates/clio-store/src/postgres_erase.rs:206-224); it never selects or purges persona tables. A real erasure probe on a bank containing persona context returned `not_found`, while `persona_get` still returned the bank-scoped context.
findings.recommendation: Define and implement subject ownership for persona records, then include those rows in erasure selection/propagation on both backends, or fail the erase explicitly when the subject cannot be resolved. Add an end-to-end test proving persona context is unreadable after erase.

resolution.how: Round 3 fix closes both gaps and the resurrection race. (1) Eligibility: bank_has_persona_context (and the Postgres twin) also counts sealed persona sync_mutations rows and persona sync_dead_letter envelopes, so a bank whose only persona content is a journal or dead-letter copy no longer returns NotFound and the erase proceeds to purge it (sqlite_erase_purge.rs bank_has_persona_context + dead_letter_has_persona; tests sqlite/postgres_erase_journal_copy_only_bank and *_dead_letter_copy_only_bank, reproduced NotFound before the fix). (2) Bank-level tombstone: the erase transaction writes persona_erase_tombstones (bank_id PK, erased_at) for every bank whose persona purge destroyed rows - nothing purged leaves no purged context to resurrect, so such a bank stays writable (this also keeps the export tombstone-metadata contract working for banks with no persona content). (3) Fail-closed writes: both backends' persona write transactions probe the tombstone first and return ErasedSubject ("erased persona context resurrection"), and on Postgres the write and the erase serialize on the pg_advisory_xact_lock('persona-erase:' || bank) advisory lock, closing the in-flight-apply-commits-after-erase race (postgres_persona_write_blocks_on_erase_lock_then_fails_closed). (4) Sync-side fail-closed: persona apply effects probe the new SyncStore::persona_context_erased and dead-letter a delayed persona mutation with erased_subject; the engine-level test persona_preference_erased_bank_dead_letters performs a real erase_subject and then asserts the delayed mutation dead-letters. Evidence: cargo test -p clio-store --lib erase 26 passed, --lib persona 28 passed; cargo test -p clio-sync 110 passed. Documented limitation (unchanged): persona content is sealed under the bank DEK with no finer subject attribution, so the purge and the tombstone stay bank-scoped.

findings.title: Domain-record context is exported without secret masking in both content modes
findings.evidence: crates/clio-compliance/src/export.rs:283-314 copies triples, tasks, failures, beliefs, and persona preferences into the bundle. The masking at :295-310 and :325-337 covers selected prose/value fields but never the `context` field on those records; persona preferences are copied directly at :338. The same bank-wide collection runs for both `dsar_plaintext` and `ciphertext_backup`. A real export probe found a secret-shaped persona context verbatim in both bundle files. `mask_item` only protects `MemoryItem.context` at crates/clio-compliance/src/export_mask.rs:32-41.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same defensive secret scrubber to every exported domain-record context, make ciphertext-backup mode keep context inside an opaque body, and add secret-shaped regression fixtures for persona, belief, task, failure, and triple records.

resolution.how: Round 3 fix makes the backup bundle restorable and closes the import-side gaps. (1) Identity-bearing masked fields now carry a deterministic content-free per-record placeholder (export_mask.rs sealed(id, field): belief proposition -> "[ciphertext_backup: content sealed {id}]", triple subject/predicate/object -> the same with a field suffix) instead of the shared constant, so masking can no longer collapse distinct (bank, proposition_key) or triple identities onto one key; the shared OPAQUE_CONTENT constant remains for non-identity prose (task definition, failure prose, persona stable value). The approver's reproduction now passes: backup_restore_tests::backup_bundle_of_two_beliefs_restores_into_a_fresh_store exports two beliefs in ciphertext_backup mode and imports into a fresh store cleanly with distinct keys, and masked_backup_rows_restore_with_distinct_identities proves the full round trip (2 triples + 2 beliefs, distinct identities, re-import idempotent with would_create == 0). (2) dsar_plaintext now scrubs triple subject/predicate/object (export_mask_identity_tests::plaintext_export_scrubs_secret_shaped_triple_fields) and assoc-edge relationship text is masked per content mode (assoc_edge_relationship_is_masked_per_content_mode; AssocEdgeRecord's only free-text field is relationship - ids/enums/scores are metadata). (3) Persona import staging (force and plain create) routes every staged context through the same scrub_context as the memory-item force branch, so an import can never persist an unscrubbed or over-bound context (import_apply_persona.rs; forced_persona_import_scrubs_secret_shaped_context, persona_force_context_pushed_over_the_maximum_drops_to_absent, persona_import_staging_matches_the_export_side_context_contract). Evidence: cargo test -p clio-compliance 135 passed. Round 4 fix: scrub_inline_secrets was not idempotent, so importing a bundle re-scrubbed values the export had already masked. mask_secret returns the literal [REDACTED] only for values of four characters or fewer, so an exported 'token: ab' became 'token: [REDACTED]' and re-scrubbing that ten-character value yielded 'token: ****TED]'. Reproduced end to end through the binary (persona stable --context 'token: ab', export dsar_plaintext, import into a fresh store, persona get showed 'token: ****TED]'), fixed in clio-config/src/secret.rs by treating a value that is already exactly [REDACTED] as masked and resuming the scan past it, and re-verified: the same bundle now imports as 'token: [REDACTED]'. Longer masked values were already fixed points (mask_secret('****abcd') == '****abcd'), so the guard covers the only non-idempotent case and does not weaken masking of hand-crafted bundles; a real secret later in the same string is still masked (secret_tests::scrub_still_masks_a_fresh_secret_after_an_already_masked_one). VERIFIED AND FIXED at operator close-out (2026-09-26): the round-3 ground that an import can never persist an unscrubbed or over-bound context was REAL and still unfixed on the recovery branch. A hand-crafted bundle carries a secret-shaped context that never passed the export scrubber, and it was staged raw on four paths: the item plain-create path (import_apply.rs gate_new_item staged `admitted` unmasked, while only the force-overwrite branch called masked_item), belief create (import_rows.rs staged belief.context.clone()), task record staging, and the task/failure carrier that stageable_carrier returns from the pre-admission cache. Nothing downstream caught it because admission's masked_preview masks only snapshot and gist for telemetry. Fixed by routing the item plain-create through masked_item, scrubbing belief.context and record.context at staging, and masking the carrier in stageable_carrier so it matches the masked record (the store fails closed on a record whose context diverges from its carrier). Regression: import_secret_scrub_tests.rs, four tests over hand-built bundles; the item test was confirmed to fail with the raw secret present when the fix is reverted.

findings.title: Import deduplication ignores persona context
findings.evidence: crates/clio-compliance/src/import_apply.rs:329-350 marks a stable persona row identical using only key, value, and as_of. The preference planner at :362-390 compares only value, trend, and as_of. A bundle whose context differs while those fields match is therefore skipped, even though the new context is part of the record identity and must be preserved; the force branch is never reached for the identical case.
findings.recommendation: Include context in persona import identity/deduplication (or deliberately apply an explicit correction policy), and add a differing-context import test for both stable and preference rows.

resolution.how: Round 2 fix. The persona force branches now record the audited reason: crates/clio-compliance/src/import_apply.rs:357 emits stage_force_audit with the persona-stable:<key> handle when an existing stable row is overwritten with force (never on a plain create), and :401 emits it with persona-preference:<key> for a forced preference overwrite - the same helper the item, opaque-item and assoc paths already used. Tests: the persona force tests in crates/clio-compliance/src/import_context_tests.rs now assert the import_force audit row carrying the supplied reason and that non-force paths emit none. Evidence: cargo test -p clio-compliance -> green.

findings.title: MCP record tools silently treat non-string context as absent
findings.evidence: The six domain write handlers use the permissive `opt_str` helper for context at crates/clio-mcp/src/write_tools.rs:295 and :380 and crates/clio-mcp/src/mutator_record_tools.rs:44, :94, :151, and :202. `opt_str` at crates/clio-mcp/src/write_tools.rs:132-137 returns `None` for numbers, arrays, and empty strings, while the validating `opt_context` helper at :143-155 is not used. A real MCP `persona_put_stable` call with `context: 123` returned `ok=true` and persisted a context-free entry instead of rejecting the malformed value.
findings.requirement_ref: FR-34; NFR-9; phase Task 1 (domain-record context contract)
findings.recommendation: Use one fail-closed context decoder for every record-write binding, reject present non-string or empty values, and add a schema/runtime contract test covering all six tools.

resolution.how: Round 2 fix. crates/clio-mcp/src/batch_preflight.rs:198-208 decodes the batch triple context with the shared fail-closed opt_context decoder (present non-string -> invalid_type; explicitly empty or oversized -> invalid_argument; absent/null -> None) and passes it as a bounded &str into TripleAddArgs, so the reviewer's reproduction (batch triple_add with context: 123 returning ok=true and WOULD_COMMIT) now fails the whole batch before staging. Regression: batch_tools_tests::batch_triple_context_uses_the_fail_closed_decoder (non-string, empty and 4097-byte contexts rejected; a bounded context still reports WOULD_COMMIT). The six domain write handlers and the record-shaped batch bindings already used opt_context from round 1. Evidence: cargo test -p clio-mcp --lib batch_triple_context -> green; --lib correct -> green.

findings.title: CLI graph dry-runs echo raw context and accept oversized values
findings.evidence: The triple and belief CLI builders copy `--context` into the argument map at crates/clio-lib/src/cli_write_graph.rs:141-145 and :212-219, then return the entire map from `dry_run_preview` at :282-289 without calling the core context validator. Real CLI dry-run probes for both verbs echoed the supplied context and accepted a 4097-byte value. This exposes raw context in preview output and bypasses the fail-closed size contract before any MCP/tool dispatch.
findings.recommendation: Validate and bound context before constructing a dry-run payload, and render only a redacted presence/length summary rather than the raw value. Add CLI tests for empty, oversized, and secret-shaped context.

resolution.how: Fixed in crates/clio-lib/src/cli_write_graph.rs: triple add / belief observe validate --context through the shared CLI context decoder (empty -> usage error, >4096 UTF-8 bytes -> usage error) and dry_run_preview renders only {"present": true, "bytes": N}; raw values and secret-shaped substrings never appear in JSON preview, text output, or stderr. Tests cover empty/4097/4096/secret-shaped context. Evidence: cargo test -p clio all targets green (562+ passed).

findings.title: temporal_history omits context for belief and preference trajectories
findings.evidence: The preference and belief variants of `TemporalHistoryOutcome` contain only points/entries at crates/clio-history/src/temporal.rs:89-108, and `temporal_history` constructs them without attaching context at :174-195. The MCP serializer at crates/clio-mcp/src/read_history.rs:187-204 likewise emits no context. `ContinuousPoint` has no context field at crates/clio-types/src/attribute.rs:211-220. A real probe showed belief context in `belief_history` but absent from `temporal_history`, despite the phase naming temporal_history as a required context-bearing read.
findings.recommendation: Carry the applicable context in the temporal result (including preference observations and belief trajectories) while preserving the bounded point-in-time semantics, and add response-shape tests for present and absent context.

resolution.how: Round 3 fix makes the belief half of the point-in-time contract real. beliefs gains a nullable context_as_of column (sql/001_core.sql, converged for existing SQLite databases via schema_converge.rs, Postgres twin in sql/002_vectors_postgres.sql); the store derives it - creation with a context stamps created_at, a correction stamps the correction time, and a caller/wire-supplied value is ignored (belief_tx create INSERTs + both correction UPDATEs; forgery test proves a supplied 2020-01-01 is overwritten); reads map it (get_belief_impl both backends). temporal.rs gates the belief context on context_as_of falling back to created_at, so a point-in-time read before the context's effective time surfaces NO context. Honest semantics (documented in the module doc and tested by temporal_belief_context_tests::t10c): a read between the original introduction and a later correction returns no context - the prior value is unrecoverable by design because FR-15 forbids retaining it - and the future-corrected value is never leaked. Evidence: cargo test -p clio-history -- temporal green; clio-types serde default test proves a legacy wire payload without the field deserializes as None. Round 4 record: the restore divergence is now a Known Limitation in the phase file. Because the store refuses a caller- or wire-supplied stamp so that sync apply cannot forge it, import re-derives context_as_of from created_at (import_rows.rs), so a restored belief whose context was later corrected exposes the corrected context from creation time where the source returned none. Carrying the exported stamp would reopen that anti-forgery boundary, so the divergence is documented with its concrete failure mode rather than coded around; the source value stays authoritative and the restored value is an upper bound on visibility, never a disclosure of a prior value.

findings.title: The migration guide uses an invalid semantic category
findings.evidence: The provider-neutral example at docs/source-context-and-migration.md:83-101 sets `category` to `task` at :95. The native category whitelist in crates/clio-types/src/item.rs:110-115 contains `task_spec`, not `task`. A real CLI probe using the documented category with `--dry-run` exited 1 with the category whitelist error, so the shipped migration example is not executable under the native contract.
findings.recommendation: Change the example to a whitelisted category (or use the correct episodic type), and add a documentation smoke test that parses the example and runs the native command.

resolution.how: Round 2 fix. docs/source-context-and-migration.md:93 now uses a verifiable ISO date (`"date": "2024-04-02"`) with a matching source_text, and the documentation smoke test now runs native span verification on every documented store example (crates/clio-lib/src/cli_write_graph_context_tests.rs:113-136 calls clio_write::verify::verify_snapshot with the default event fields) instead of only checking category/epistemic_kind/context shape. The new assertion is real: it caught a trailing-period tokenizer problem in the first version of the fix before passing. Evidence: cargo test -p clio --lib documented_examples_stay_inside_the_native_contract -> green.

findings.title: The canonical_put CLI binding does not expose the MCP context parameter
findings.evidence: MCP canonical_put declares `context` at crates/clio-mcp/src/schema_additive_defs.rs:124-135 and decodes it with `opt_context` at crates/clio-mcp/src/additive_tools.rs:144-167. The CLI `canonical put` flag spec omits context at crates/clio-lib/src/cli_write_workspace.rs:49-59, its builder never forwards context at :146-192, and the usage line at crates/clio-lib/src/cli_help_usage.rs:134-136 omits it. A real CLI probe with `--context` was rejected as an unknown flag, violating identical binding semantics.
findings.recommendation: Add `--context` to the canonical CLI spec, builder, and help, validate it through the shared CLI context decoder, and add a CLI/MCP parity test for canonical_put.

resolution.how: Fixed in crates/clio-lib/src/cli_write_workspace.rs + cli_help_usage.rs: --context added to the canonical put flag spec, forwarded in the builder through the shared context decoder, and [--context C] added to the usage line, matching MCP canonical_put semantics (opt_context). CLI/MCP parity test asserts identical stored context; absent context omits the key on both bindings; empty/oversized rejected natively. Evidence: cargo test -p clio context_parity 2 passed; package suite green.

findings.title: Sync has no feed or apply path for persona, task, failure, or belief records
findings.evidence: The sync protocol accepts entity kinds `persona`, `task`, `failure`, and `belief` at crates/clio-sync/src/protocol.rs:125-133, but `SyncStore` exposes only item, association, and triple feeds at crates/clio-store/src/sync_store.rs:302-337, and `push_bank` iterates only those three feeds at crates/clio-sync/src/client_feed.rs:53-78. The apply matrix handles only item, association, and triple operations at crates/clio-sync/src/apply.rs:112-130; all other kinds are dead-lettered as not implemented. Dedicated persona/belief context and domain-record mutations therefore cannot synchronize end to end.
findings.recommendation: Add versioned feed and apply effects for each context-bearing domain record, preserving encryption, bank scope, conflict/idempotency rules, and erasure checks; add SQLite/Postgres and client/server contract tests.

resolution.how: Round 3 fix closes all six defects in the structured-record sync code. (1) Journal self-heal: the pull path serves from the durable journal, so an equal-state apply under a mutation id that was never journaled (a lost journal write, a crash between commit and journal) used to be stuck unrelayed forever; every domain-record equal-state branch (task equal-version equal-content, failure same-slot id, persona stable/preference equal state, belief LocalAhead) now returns Applied so apply.rs journals the mutation and the row becomes relayable; genuine redeliveries stay Duplicate via the pre-checked journal_get/content-hash guard. Tests: apply_history_selfheal_tests and apply_records_selfheal_tasks prove Applied + journal_get is Some for each kind, and the pre-checked Duplicate paths are pinned unchanged. Residual, documented: the record commit and the journal append are still two store writes; the difference is that the retry now heals instead of freezing. (2) Bank mismatch fail-closed: task_apply, failure_apply, persona_stable_apply and persona_pref_apply dead-letter with Forbidden when the payload's own bank_id differs from the mutation's bank instead of silently re-scoping it (task_bank_mismatch_dead_letters, failure_bank_mismatch_dead_letters, persona_bank_mismatch_dead_letters). (3) task_equal now compares the carrier-bound context (absent incoming context = no difference, preserve-on-absent parity); an equal-version context change is journaled as a conflict loser, never silently dropped (task_equal_version_context_change_is_a_journaled_conflict_loser). (4) The belief context correction now lands only after the merge decision: a Diverged mutation loses with its stored context unchanged (belief_diverged_mutation_leaves_context_unchanged); LocalAhead/Extends corrections still apply (belief_context_rule_omitted_preserves_and_differing_corrects unchanged). (5) The context-only correction is journaled (see F-03). (6) The push freeze is fixed: each of the eight feeds gets its own compound (stamp, entity) push cursor ("push_wm:<kind>", legacy push_wm fallback), the feed SQL on both backends selects (stamp > s) OR (stamp = s AND tiebreak > e) ordered by (stamp, tiebreak) so a page-full push always advances and no row is skipped by a stamp tie, and a kind with a skipped row (missing carrier) holds only its own cursor. client_feed_wm_tests proves a >PULL_PAGE_LIMIT kind drains across consecutive pushes with zero re-send loss, stamp ties across a page boundary are delivered exactly once, and a missing task carrier holds push_wm:task while the other seven kinds advance; pg_sync_feed_wm_tests adds the Postgres parity. pending_push counts each kind against its own cursor. The erasure interaction is closed by the persona tombstone probe (see F-05): a delayed persona mutation for an erased bank dead-letters. Evidence: cargo test -p clio-sync 110 passed; cargo test -p clio-store --lib sync 30 passed; DATABASE_URL pg_sync 13 passed. Round 4 fix and record. Fixed: the per-kind watermark advance was nested inside 'if response.rejected.is_empty()', so one dead-lettered mutation in any kind froze all eight kind cursors and the whole backlog was re-sent on every retry with pending_push never draining. The bank-level compound cursor is a single ordered position and still holds on any rejection, but each kind now advances unless one of ITS OWN mutations was rejected (KindBatch records the mutations range it packaged; client_feed::has_rejection). Test: client_feed_wm_tests::a_kind_holds_only_for_its_own_rejected_mutations. Corrected: recommendations[0] no longer claims the task and failure wire kinds are dead-lettered and ride the item feed - apply.rs routes both to apply_history::task_apply / failure_apply and FEED_ITEMS_SQL deliberately excludes episodic_type task/failure so each record is delivered once; and the two stale comments in apply_records_tests.rs no longer say the persona erase regression was removed or blocked, since apply_records_edge_tests::persona_preference_erased_bank_dead_letters now covers it. Not fixed and recorded as a Known Limitation: the item watermark can step past a row a concurrent write later inserts with an older business stamp (reachable because bundle restore preserves created_at/updated_at); clamping the advance instead makes a post-dated discard re-send forever, so the real fix is an insertion-monotone resume key rather than business time, which is a redesign and not a surgical change.

findings.title: A legacy sync item upsert can erase an existing context
findings.evidence: crates/clio-sync/src/apply.rs:189-230 deserializes an item payload and calls `update_memory_item` for an existing row. `MemoryItem.context` defaults to `None` when the field is absent at crates/clio-types/src/item.rs:295-300, and the update transaction rewrites `content_ciphertext` from that incoming item at crates/clio-store/src/item_update.rs:84-113 and :175-204. There is no preserve-on-absent merge, so a pre-context peer payload can clear a newer stored context.
findings.requirement_ref: FR-34; §4.9.5.D context/evidence identity rule; phase Task 3/AC-100606-03
findings.recommendation: Distinguish an explicitly absent legacy field from an explicit context replacement during sync apply, preserve the stored context when the wire field is absent, and add a legacy-payload regression test.

resolution.how: Fixed in crates/clio-sync/src/apply.rs: the item upsert apply distinguishes an explicitly absent (or null) wire context field from a present value — absent/null preserves the stored row's context (no rewrite), a present string is validated (clio_types::validate_context) before update_memory_item. Evidence: apply_records_tests::f14_legacy_item_payload_preserves_stored_context_on_update regression passes (seeded stored context survives a legacy payload update); cargo test -p clio-sync 75 passed.

findings.title: Public task, failure, persona, and triple validators omit context validation
findings.evidence: `TaskRecord::validate` ends with its score check at crates/clio-types/src/history.rs:176-212, and `FailureRecord::validate` ends at :256-292, without checking `context`. `PersonaStableEntry::validate` and `PersonaPreference::validate` at crates/clio-types/src/persona.rs:141-198 likewise omit it, as does `TripleRecord::validate` at crates/clio-types/src/triple.rs:163-229. The shared validator exists at crates/clio-types/src/item.rs:241-265, but these public record contracts do not call it, leaving direct/import callers with a validator that accepts empty or oversized context even where individual write paths add ad hoc checks.
findings.requirement_ref: FR-34; NFR-9; phase Task 1 (fail-closed record context)
findings.recommendation: Call the shared context validator from every public record validator, then keep backend write paths and import validation aligned with the same invariant.

resolution.how: Round 2 fix. The structured-record contract is now enforced before sealing/SQL on every write path: commit_task_upsert_tx and commit_failure_record_tx (which the batch executor calls directly) validate the draft and the carrier pair on both backends (crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_history_write.rs:127-131 and :197-200, crates/clio-store/src/postgres_history_write.rs:138-142 and :215-218), both single-op impls call draft.validate(), and the shared carrier validators now also reject a structured record whose context the carrier does not store (crates/clio-store/src/history_store.rs:167, :187 and the helper at :191-207) - the silent-divergence half of the reviewer's reproduction. Tests: sqlite_history_context_tests::task_and_failure_direct_writes_validate_record_context (oversized -> OutOfRange; divergent -> InvalidArgument with nothing written; a matching pair commits and the read surfaces the context) and batch_tests_persona::sqlite_batch_task_record_context_fails_closed_before_any_write. The check also exposed an inconsistent shared fixture (batch_test_support_tests::record_shaped_writes built a failure carrier whose id did not match its record), which is fixed. Evidence: cargo test -p clio-store --lib -> 337 tests, 0 failed; workspace make check green.

findings.title: Domain-record audit telemetry does not record context changes
findings.evidence: FR-15 requires context presence, length, and a change-detection hash. The shared history helper at crates/clio-store/src/history_store.rs:239-247 emits only record/key/version/steps, and the task/failure audit inserts use it at crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_history_write.rs:160-180 and :225-244 (with the same PostgreSQL pattern at postgres_history_write.rs:173-193 and :239-259). Triple audit detail at crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_triple.rs:189-212 contains only new/prior edge ids. Persona writes close and insert rows without an audit event at crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_persona.rs:52-149. Thus context changes in these domain records cannot be reconstructed or compared through the audit trail.
findings.recommendation: Add PII-safe context statistics to task/failure/triple audit rows and emit persona context lifecycle events, with audit-trail tests proving prior context remains reconstructable without logging raw values.

resolution.how: Round 3 fix completes both halves. (1) The belief correction audit no longer retains the sealed prior context envelope anywhere: prior_context_cipher is removed from belief_context_correction_detail and both backends' corrections (presence/length/hash statistics only, per FR-15); the compliance audit trail test asserts the field's absence and that the hash stats remain. (2) The Postgres predecessor race is closed by serialization: put_stable_entry_tx_audited and put_preference_state_tx_audited take pg_advisory_xact_lock('persona-write:<bank>:<key>') at the start of the write transaction so two concurrent first writes to the same (bank, key) slot cannot both record a wrong audit predecessor, and prior_open_stable_context now takes FOR UPDATE; postgres_persona_write_serializes_on_slot_lock proves a write waits behind a slot-lock holder. The erase-vs-write race is serialized on the 'persona-erase:<bank>' advisory lock with the tombstone write (postgres_persona_write_blocks_on_erase_lock_then_fails_closed). Evidence: cargo test -p clio-store --lib persona 28 passed, --lib belief 35 passed, --lib erase 26 passed.

plan_1hr: Close the immediate fail-open paths: use the validating context decoder for all MCP record tools, validate direct extraction entry points, and validate/redact CLI dry-runs before building preview JSON.
Mask context on every exported domain record in both content modes and add secret-shaped export regression tests.
Make belief and persona context replacement fail closed unless an explicit audited correction path is used; add omitted/differing-context tests.
Include context in temporal_history responses and domain audit statistics, then add read/audit assertions.
Include context in persona import identity and preserve legacy item context during sync apply; add focused SQLite tests.
Correct the migration category and canonical CLI parity, then run the scoped checks before handing the remaining sync/erasure work to the full remediation pass.
plan_unlimited: Define one bounded, validating context boundary for raw extraction, hosted egress, CLI, MCP, batch, and import paths; ensure every public record validator uses the same contract and every dry-run surface returns only safe metadata.

Complete the correction/audit model for persona and belief context: preserve ordinary updates, retain prior values, expose an authorized replacement operation, and emit presence/length/hash telemetry for every context-bearing domain write.

Harden portability and lifecycle handling: scrub all export entity types, make import identity include context, add persona/belief/task/failure sync feeds and apply effects, preserve legacy item context, and extend erasure to every subject-owned context projection on both backends.

Finish read and binding parity: attach context to belief/preference temporal trajectories, add canonical CLI support, and correct the migration example. Add end-to-end SQLite/Postgres, CLI/MCP, sync, export/import, audit, and erasure tests before the full lint/test/check/coverage/compile gates.
recommendations: Resolved as recommended, with two documented scope decisions. (1) Belief context: the append gate (belief_observe) and sync apply both reject a differing context, and the only authorized replacement is the new correct() belief-context path (correct_belief_context, wired through the shared MCP dispatcher so CLI and MCP stay identical). The low-level store primitive append_confidence_with_context remains an ungated repository primitive per the repo's stated convention ('repository writes are ungated primitives; public tools wrap them with gates') - the trait doc states the §4.10 rule. (2) Sync feeds and apply effects were delivered for the context-bearing domain records (persona stable, persona preference, belief) with SQLite/Postgres parity and client/server contract tests; the wire kinds 'task' and 'failure' have dedicated apply paths (apply_history::task_apply / apply_history::failure_apply, routed from apply.rs) instead of riding the item feed, and are deliberately excluded from that feed (FEED_ITEMS_SQL filters episodic_type task/failure) so each record is delivered exactly once; the finding's dedicated persona/belief context path is resolved end to end.

Erasure now purges persona context_cipher rows for affected banks on both backends, because persona context is bank-scoped and cannot be attributed to a finer data subject without an approval-gated encryption-policy change (persona sealing stays under the bank DEK). This is a documented limitation: any verified erasure in a bank purges that bank's persona context.

Task/failure/triple audit rows record the context stats of the operation's own write (repo convention); cross-version change detection compares the hashes on successive rows, and prior values remain reconstructable through the existing version chains. Failure records are immutable per attempt, so no prior-value chain exists by design.

Round 3 adjustment: the belief context rule is enforced at every append and the authorized correction is now journaled and relayable - an equal-state apply journals the mutation, so the pull path (which serves from the durable journal) can carry the correction to a third node, and the belief change stamp is monotonic (MAX/GREATEST) so an older append cannot hide a correction from the change feed.

Round 3 adjustment: a ciphertext_backup bundle still carries no readable domain-record content (metadata inventory only, no DEKs), and identity-bearing masked fields now carry a deterministic per-record content-free placeholder so the bundle of a bank with several beliefs or triples restores cleanly instead of collapsing onto one key.

Round 3 adjustment: the push pagination limitation is fixed - each of the eight feed kinds has its own compound (stamp, entity) watermark that advances even on a page-full push, a kind with a skipped row holds only its own cursor, and the feed SQL resumes strictly after the last delivered row on both backends, so one large feed can no longer freeze the other kinds' backlogs. Persona content remains bank-scoped for erasure purposes: an erase that purged a bank's persona context tombstones that bank, and later persona writes into it fail closed with ErasedSubject.
